title: Assigning a lead to unassigned work moves only open unassigned lines
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 2 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Ralph Edwards", "Dana Ortiz"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Dana Ortiz") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  6. Create a new work order on this build for the case customer with no lead technician (e.g. "S1-710").
    • Add "Line 1 Unassigned" with no technician.
    • Add "Line 2 Explicit" and in Edit Line set Technicians = "Dana Ortiz".
    • Add "Line 3 Complete" with no technician, approve it, enter a tech story and complete it.
    • Approve the other lines (the work order reads Approved).
    • Write down each line's Labor row: Line 1 Unassigned, Line 2 Dana Ortiz, Line 3 Unassigned (Complete).
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; in the design its button tooltip reads "Board").
  2. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  3. Hover the card in the Unassigned column, click More actions > Reassign lead technician.
  4. Pick Ralph Edwards and confirm.
  5. Open the work order's Lines tab and read each line's Labor row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The card moves to Ralph Edwards' column with "Lead technician updated".
  • Line 1 now shows Ralph Edwards. Line 2 still shows Dana Ortiz. Line 3 (Complete) still reads Unassigned. So 1 of 3 lines moved.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R8 (assign path), read 8 Oct 2026. PRD acceptance note under the S4-R8 table (all six rows for assign, reassign and remove). Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R8: “Apply the line-movement rules below on every path that assigns, changes, or removes the lead technician.”
  • S4-R8 acceptance: “Acceptance criteria must cover all six rows for assign, reassign and remove. Any No condition overrides a Yes condition.”
  • S4-R8 table: no technician: “Has no technician assigned | Yes”
  • S4-R8 table: explicit: “Explicitly assigned to a different technician | No — the explicit assignment is preserved”
  • S4-R8 table: Complete: “Status is Complete | No”
